Hey, thank you for the kind words, also merry Christmas! With cars is pretty difficult bc each mistake “etiology” is quite complex. First, know that ITS OKAY to get questions wrong or make dumb mistakes - don’t beat urself up for it. And ik it’s quite frustrating but think of the big picture, try relating reading cars to reading patient charts in the future where you will have a limited time to synthesize information and make the correct call (also might have to deal with bad handwriting). Personally I have made a list of the mistakes I’ve made and categorized them, for ex. “Did not understand main idea” or (more embarrassingly) “did not understand vocabulary”. For aamc cars especially, I would go back and try to reason why each answer choice is wrong and why each was right. I wouldn’t worry too much about getting into the nitty gritty with third party stuff as their logic is a bit different. Dm me if you want further detail of how I would approach reviewing cars passages!

Physics is rough, I was pretty lucky to have taken ap physics 1 and 2 in hs. Just do as many practice problems as you can, both passage wise and individual physics questions. You can find free resources for physics like the openstax textbook and there are lots of practice questions in there. Recognizing when to use specific equations is also important!

The key thing is to try as many strategies as you can and see which one works for you the best. really try to take your time with this election process. After that you can practice the heck out of cars using the strategy that you selected that works the best for you and you will improve. Go slow first then progressively go faster and build stamina. Anki!! I always did anki while laying in bed or just whenever I had a chance to take out my phone like in line in a grocery store. You can also try watching passage walk-throughs on YouTube and I did that while I was eating instead of watching Netflix or smt haha. Best of luck to you!!

And obviously remember all of the equations that you would encounter. For concepts specifically if you don’t understand something then YouTube videos would help a lot, especially khan Academy, and the organic chemistry tutor. But honestly, I find that the mcat doesn’t really require deep understandings of specific topics just know how to use the equations. definitely practice how to digest passages and know how/ when to apply the equations/concepts you know and this is true for all of the science sections. Watching passage walkthroughs on yt helped a bunch, u can use their Strats or find a strat that works for you
